title: Shilpa Gupta: What Still Holds
description: Starting point of Shilpa Gupta’s solo exhibition at Hamburger Bahnhof is the monumental work Truth, situated at the intersection of language, power, and control.

title: Intermezzo: Revisiting Helmut Newton
venue: Museum für Fotografie - Helmut Newton Stiftung
description: The new permanent exhibition at the Museum of Photography will respond even more dynamically to the different aspects of Helmut and June Newton's photographic works.

title: Ruin and Rush: Berlin 1910–1930
description: With the exhibition Ruin and Rush, the Neue Nationalgalerie focuses on selected works from its collection of Classical Modernism that address the Berlin of the 1910s and 1920s.

title: Lina Lapelytė: We Make Years Out of Hours – Chanel Commission
description: For the second edition of the Chanel Commission Lina Lapelytė will transform the Historic Hall into a polyphonic stage for a participatory choreography.

title: Rooftop Screening: City Fragments
description: Manually curated screening added as a fallback example without prefilled coordinates.

title: Rooms / Stages
venue: Museum für Fotografie - Helmut Newton Stiftung
description: The exhibition “Rooms / Stages” dispenses with artistic documentation, instead shifting the context and focus from the performative act to the stage space itself.

title: Gabriele Stötzer: Dabei sein und nicht schweigen
description: For over five decades, Gabriele Stötzer has been addressing issues such as justice, self-determination, and gender.

title: Materialistin: Matter of Care, Care of Matter
description: The exhibition features sculptures and site-specific installations at the Hamburger Bahnhof that explore social and cultural-political issues.

title: Everybody
description: The artworks on display focus on the body not as a static category, but as a dynamic construct shaped by social, historical, and emotional influences.

title: Josef Kaiser: Building for the GDR
description: Josef Kaiser is considered one of the most influential architects of the GDR. For the first time, this exhibition explores his life and work through drawings, photographs, films, and models, shedding light on political and aesthetic tensions.

title: Zwischen Bäumen
description: At Villa Schöningen, some 90 works by more than 60 international artists spanning three centuries explore the forest as a motif, a space of memory, and a cultural canvas.

title: Kreuzberg
description: In 2026, the exhibition “Kreuzberg” will be dedicated to the diverse and hitherto largely unrecognized cultural production surrounding the theme of labor migration, showing how artists in Kreuzberg are addressing the tensions and issues of their time.

title: Maurizio Cattelan: Night – Preis der Nationalgalerie 2026
description: The Italian artist Maurizio Cattelan is one of the most influential positions in contemporary art and has been awarded the Preis der Nationalgalerie 2026.

title: Ryuichi Sakamoto: seeing sound, hearing time
description: The composer and artist Ryuichi Sakamoto is considered a pioneer of electronic and experimental music who has constantly redefined the boundaries between sound, film, performance and visual art.

title: The Magic of the Street
description: Masterpieces of Street Photography: The exhibition "The Magic of the Street" presents some of the most important names in the history of photography.

title: Nizo Yamamoto: Master of Anime Scenography
description: Yamamoto is considered one of the most influential art directors in Japanese animated film. For more than four decades, he created visual worlds that have left a lasting mark on the visual memory of the genre.

title: Christoph Schlingensief: Es ist nicht mehr mein Problem, macht eure Scheiße alleine
description: The Gropius Bau is dedicating an exhibition to Schlingensief that highlights his visionary work, ranging from sensational political actions and radical theatrical productions to the fusion of performance and visual art.

title: Lovis Corinth: Then came Berlin!
description: It is hard to exaggerate Lovis Corinth’s contribution to modernism. In his own lifetime the virtuosic painter (1858–1925) was one of the most eminent and influential figures in the Berlin art world.

title: Next Door: Tacita Dean and Bruce Nauman, Thomas Demand, Olafur Eliasson, Henrik Håkansson, Tomás Saraceno
description: The group exhibition underscores the ongoing creative relevance of this unique site.

title: Susan Hiller: Bad Dreams
description: Susan Hiller's first retrospective exhibition in Berlin presents hypnotic and phantasmagorical audiovisual works alongside sculptures made from collected everyday objects and images from the internet, film, and television.

title: Genghis Khan: The world of the Mongols
description: The Museum of Prehistory and Early History is focusing on Genghis Khan as a central ruling figure in a major exhibition and shedding archaeological light on the world of the Mongols, which is virtually unknown in this country.

title: Across Epochs: Gursky, Lucas, Miró, Warhol and the Art of the Long 19th Century
description: In the special presentation at the Alte Nationalgalerie, works by artists from the 19th and late 20th centuries are brought together in select locations throughout the building.

title: Roger Ballen: roger ballen.! drawing meets photography
description: The exhibition “roger ballen.! drawing meets photography” explores the fluid boundaries between drawing, photography, and painting.

title: Swedish modernism
description: In cooperation with Moderna Museet, Stockholm, the Brücke Museum is presenting a comprehensive exhibition on Swedish modernism for the first time in Germany.
